CheckTitle: Ensure IAM roles used by AWS services include aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount conditions to prevent confused deputy attacks
Description: IAM roles whose trust policies allow AWS service principals (e.g., lambda.amazonaws.com, ec2.amazonaws.com) to assume them should include aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount, or aws:SourceOrgID conditions. Without these conditions, any resource in any account using that service could potentially assume the role.
Risk: The confused deputy problem occurs when a service principal can be tricked into performing actions on behalf of a different customer's resource. Without source ARN conditions, a malicious actor controlling a resource in another account could potentially leverage the service to assume your role.
Remediation: Add aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount conditions to trust policies for service-principal roles. See AWS documentation on confused deputy prevention for service-specific recommended conditions.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM documentation — confused deputy problem prevention; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC-11 (Trusted Path), AC-4 (Information Flow Enforcement); cross-service confused deputy is an AWS-documented attack vector
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM documentation — Preventing confused deputy problem; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — confused deputy prevention is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
